steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add egg noodles and cook until the pasta is tender yet firm to the bite, about 5 minutes; drain.

Meanwhile, melt butter in a large skillet over low heat. Add cabbage and season with salt and pepper. Cover and cook until the cabbage begins to brown, 5 to 7 minutes. Add cooked noodles; cook and stir until the noodles begin to brown, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Fried Cabbage and Egg Noodles
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for fried cabbage and noodles calls for the cabbage to be browned in lots of butter. Simple yet delicious with just a few ingredients!
raw_recipe.name: Fried Cabbage and Egg Noodles

recipeInstructions.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add egg noodles and cook until the pasta is tender yet firm to the bite, about 5 minutes; drain.

Meanwhile, melt butter in a large skillet over low heat. Add cabbage and season with salt and pepper. Cover and cook until the cabbage begins to brown, 5 to 7 minutes. Add cooked noodles; cook and stir until the noodles begin to brown, about 5 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This was delicious! I cut up an onion and two cloves of fresh garlic which I added to the cabbage and 1/2 stick of butter. When the noodles were done, I added a tablespoon of butter to the noodles before adding them to the cabbage mixture. I will make this again and maybe cut up a small ham steak to add a little meat to this dish. Thank you for the recipe!

This is called Haluski. I make it often, but instead of buying a head of cabbage, I buy a bag of precut cole slaw..... then I fry the cole slaw cabbage in tons of butter, and onions, and add cooked noodles.

Good basic recipe. For authentic German flavor add to cabbage while cooking 1/2 Tsp. each of Caraway and Fennel seeds plus 3 or 4 crushed Juniper berries. For even more depth cook egg noodles risotto-style with your favorite broth.

We actually used spaghetti squash instead of noodles and we added onions with the fried cabbage. At the end, I added garlic powder as well as salt and pepper also. It was so delicious! We paired it with both vegetarian sausage and turkey sausage, with lots of Dijon mustard as well as hot and sweet mustard on the side. It tasted like sweet sauerkraut and was really good! We are going to make this again for sure!

I read several versions of this recipe and used thinly sliced onions, one whole stick of butter and a bag of preshredded cabbage in a big pot. The browning gives flavor and you need to stir often to keep the butter from burning. Add drained noodles when done and mix throughly. Real comfort food!!

The first time I made it I found it bland, but I decided to make it again and modify the recipe. So I added thinly sliced onions and grated carrots to the cabbage. I sautéed the veggies with caraway seed for about 5 minutes in butter and then added about 1/4 C chicken stock, covered the pan and simmered for about 5 minutes. I removed the lid and raised the temperature to reduce the liquid and brown the veggies lightly. Then I added the noodles and some leftover Octoberfest sausages and sautéed until the sausages were heated through.

I like noodles in any dish, but I think this is better, more flavorful and more nutritious when you add sautéed onions, garlic, mushrooms or any other favorite vegetables. The onions are a must, though. You could also make it a meal by adding leftover rotisserie chicken, ground beef or any other protein of your choosing.
Haluski! We have been making this for generations. We always add onions and garlic. It is great as is or add any leftover veggie or meat you may have. It's really good with cottage cheese mix in too.
I fried bacon and drained most of the drippings, added the cabbage to the drippings and simmered until cabbage was cooked. I then added the cooked noodles. Much better flavor.

Simply loved it! I took the advice from another post and added a teaspoon of Fennel and sugar to the butter before adding the cabbage. I also chopped up a onion and two cloves of garlic and added that to the cabbage . I cooked it down until nice and carmelized.. Added the cooked noodles and added salt and pepper to taste. Upon serving I sprinkled some Parmesan cheese for a little extra flavour. Will make again. Family loved it!??

Used spiral pasta and added onions, garlic, and a bit of sugar. One stick of butter is a bit much; I think you could get away with one half to 3/4 stick of butter. Unfortunately my cabbage burned a little due to faulty temp gauge on stove top. Either way, it still came out alright and will make again.
Halved the recipe. Will try less butter next time.
Pantry Friendly
I have made this often; everything is the same but I add sliced kielbasa to it and call it Haluski. I thought it was a Polish recipe! It's very good and easy to make.

We loved this recipe. Followed all directions and ingredients as stated. It will be added to our list of side dishes. You could add bacon and garlic or as others suggested, cooked potatoes, bread pieces and it would be very good. Great recipe!
This was so good! I had some homemade egg noodles left over - this was the perfect place for them. I listened to somebody else's suggestion and added garlic. We had ours with bratwurst. So good.
Delish. Used some bacon fat to replace some butter. Added onion. Very simple and filling.
This was great! Reminded me of my dad making this. He always added a little bread - broken up in pieces and buttered. Croutons work as well. It just adds another layer of flavor.

I also add large diced potatoes that I boiled firm first...salted --- Then add them last.Amount to taste. And also add a dollop of sour cream mixed in separately on a plate full. Crumpled bacon at times also---===
Excellent. I added a chopped onion and black pepper.
